items.title: The Fourfold Refutation: Not Self-Made, Not Other-Made, Not Both, Not Uncaused (continued)

items.zh: 如是由勝義故，無有宰主、作者、受者，唯有因果。於因果相釋通疑難，略由五頌，顯示於此起我顛倒。初頌顯示雖無有我，而有後有無有斷絕；又諸因果非頓俱有；非從一切一切得生；又此因道無有斷絕。頌中四句，如其次第釋此四難。由第二頌，顯因果相。由後三頌，顯於無我諸因果中起我顛倒。此中顯示彼所緣境、彼所依止、彼因、彼果。初頌顯示彼所緣境。自內所證，無色難見，難可尋思，故名無色。經說色相為尋思故；難說示他，故不可見。由第二頌，顯彼依果。凡夫是依，眾見是果。由第三頌，顯示彼因。俱生我見，由總執計自種隨眠之所生起。諸外道等分別我見，由宿習等之所生起。此外道見，要由數習故、不正尋思故，又得隨順從他聽聞非正法故，而得生長。此中顯示由所依止、作意、所緣諸過失故，分別我見方得生起。次後五頌，顯彼我見，由集次第，發生於苦；又即此苦，并及我見二苦因緣；又於解脫能為障礙。此中初頌，顯示於集；第二、第三，顯示行苦所攝阿賴耶識。愛藏此已，而趣戲論。謂我當有、非當有等。言愛藏者，攝為己體故。又復此苦，於一切時恒常隨逐，無一剎那而暫息者。由第四頌，顯示此苦是能計我及苦樂緣。由第五頌，顯示計我由愚癡故，障礙解脫。言增上者，望餘二苦故。言遍行者，隨逐諸受故。遍所作者，遍善、惡、無記故。今當顯示阿賴耶識所攝行苦共他相似。又顯差別。由正法行方能竭故，於世眾流最為暴惡。言眾流者，譬眼等六，五趣、三界等。又法行者，顯示解了解脫遍知及縛遍知。解了縛遍知者，即了知苦。謂了知我受苦受樂，皆依於苦。又此分別能起諸見；從彼所生，亦能生彼。顯示解了縛遍知已。餘有六頌，顯示解了解脫遍知。謂染污意恒時，諸惑俱生滅。若解脫諸惑，非先亦非後等。非先者，與諸煩惱恒俱生故。非後者，即與彼惑俱時滅故。又顯所說解脫之相。謂非即彼生已後方清淨，別有所餘清淨意生；即彼先來無染污故，說為解脫。為成此義，故復說言：其有染污者，畢竟性清淨等頌。又復顯示二種解脫。謂煩惱解脫及事解脫。諸種子滅故，諸煩惱盡故者，顯示煩惱解脫。即於此無染者，顯示事解脫。如經言：苾芻當知！若於眼中貪欲永斷，如是此眼亦當永斷，乃至廣說。如是顯示有餘依解脫已，次當顯示無餘依解脫。自內所證者，顯彼不思議故。「唯眾苦盡」者，為遣妄計唯無性執。謂有餘依永寂滅故，說為寂滅，非全無性。無戲論者，此解脫性唯內所證。若異不異、死後當有或當無等一切戲論不能說故。為顯補特伽羅及法，俱非流轉生死或般涅槃。故復頌言：眾生名相續，及法想相中，無生死流轉，亦無涅槃者。
items.en: Thus, ultimately, there is no ruler, agent, or experiencer; there are only cause and effect. To resolve doubts about the characteristics of cause and effect, five verses in brief show how the inversion of self arises here. The first verse shows that although there is no self, later existence is not cut off; that causes and effects do not exist all at once together; that not everything arises from everything; and that this path of causes is not cut off. The four lines of the verse answer these four difficulties in order. The second verse shows the characteristics of cause and effect. The last three verses show how the inversion of self arises among causes and effects that have no self. Here are shown its object, its support, its cause, and its result. The first verse shows its object: it is realised inwardly, formless, hard to see, and hard to reason about, so it is called formless; the sūtras speak of the characteristics of form as what is reasoned about; and because it is hard to describe to others, it is called invisible. The second verse shows its support and result: the ordinary being is the support, the many views are the result. The third verse shows its cause. The innate view of self arises from the latent tendencies of its own seeds through grasping the whole together. The discriminated view of self of non-Buddhists and others arises from past habit and the like. This non-Buddhist view grows through repeated practice, through incorrect reasoning, and through hearing from others teachings that are not the true Dharma. This shows that the discriminated view of self arises because of faults in its support, its attention, and its object. The next five verses show that this view of self gives rise to suffering through the sequence of origination; that this suffering, together with the view of self, is the condition for both kinds of suffering; and that it obstructs liberation. The first of these verses shows origination. The second and third show the ālaya-consciousness, included in the suffering of formations. Craving hoards it and then runs into elaboration, thinking 'I shall exist' or 'I shall not exist', and so on. 'Craving hoards' means it takes it as its own substance. Further, this suffering follows us at all times, constantly, not pausing for a single moment. The fourth verse shows that this suffering is the condition for imagining a self and for pain and pleasure. The fifth verse shows that imagining a self, because of delusion, obstructs liberation. 'Dominant' is said in comparison with the other two kinds of suffering. 'Pervasive' because it follows all feelings. 'Pervading what is done' because it pervades the wholesome, the unwholesome, and the indeterminate. Now it will be shown how the suffering of formations included in the ālaya-consciousness is similar to and different from others: because it can be dried up only by the practice of the true Dharma, it is the most violent of the world's floods. 'The floods' is a simile for the six, the eye and the rest, the five destinies, the three realms, and so on. Further, 'practice of the Dharma' shows understanding, full knowledge of liberation and full knowledge of bondage. Understanding full knowledge of bondage means knowing suffering: knowing that the self's experience of pain and of pleasure both depend on suffering. Further, this discrimination can give rise to views, and what is born from them can in turn give rise to it. This shows understanding full knowledge of bondage. The remaining six verses show understanding full knowledge of liberation. That is, the defiled mind always arises and ceases together with the defilements. 'If one is liberated from the defilements, it is not before and not after', and so on. 'Not before' because it always arises together with the afflictions; 'not after' because it ceases at the same time as those defilements. It also shows the characteristic of the liberation spoken of: it is not that, after it has arisen, it is then purified, and some other pure mind arises; rather, because it was not defiled from the start, it is called liberated. To establish this meaning, the next verse says, 'Whatever is defiled is ultimately pure by nature', and so on. It also shows two kinds of liberation: liberation from afflictions and liberation from things. 'Because the seeds cease and the afflictions are exhausted' shows liberation from afflictions. 'Being undefiled with regard to this' shows liberation from things. As the sūtra says: 'Monks, know that if desire for the eye is cut off for ever, then the eye too will be cut off for ever', and so on at length. Having thus shown liberation with remainder, it next shows liberation without remainder. 'Realised inwardly' shows that it is inconceivable. 'Only the end of all suffering' is said to remove the false notion that it is merely non-existence: because what remained is calmed for ever, it is called calm, not total non-existence. 'Without elaboration' means that this liberation is realised only inwardly, because no elaboration such as 'same or different' or 'it will or will not exist after death' can express it. To show that neither the person nor dharmas transmigrate in birth and death or attain parinirvāṇa, the verse says further: 'In the continuum named a being, and in the marks of dharmas, there is no transmigration in birth and death, and no one who attains nirvana.'

blocks.text: The last part of the prose commentary on the verses of non-self. **All of today's Chinese is missing from Ru-Yi's translation**; the English column gives our own translation, and the commentary summarises it. It explains verses 27–44 (Day 128).

items: **Only cause and result.** Ultimately there is no ruler, agent, or experiencer, "only cause and result". Conventionally one may say "one does and one receives"; whether doer and receiver are the same or different cannot be said.

**Four objections answered** (verse 27). Without a self: (1) rebirth still continues without break; (2) cause and result are not simultaneous; (3) not everything arises from everything; (4) the causal path is never cut. Venerable Miào Jìng: this verse answers exactly these four objections.

**How self-view arises in a selfless process** (verses 29–31). Its **object** is "known only by inner experience", formless and hard to see or explain (Venerable Miào Jìng: the manas's grasping of the ālayavijñāna). Its **support** is ordinary beings; its **result**, their many views. Its **cause**: innate self-view arises from the seeds of self-grasping; the constructed self-view of non-Buddhists arises from habit, unsound reflection, and hearing wrong teachings.

**Suffering** (verses 32–36). The ālayavijñāna, included in the suffering of formations, is "cherished" as self and drives proliferation: "I will exist; I will not exist." This suffering accompanies every moment. It is like a river that sends out many streams (the senses, the five destinies, the three realms), the most violent of the world's floods, dried up only by practice of the Dharma. Knowing bondage means seeing that "I experience pain and pleasure" all rests on suffering.

**Liberation** (verses 37–44). The defiled manas always arises and ceases together with its afflictions; liberation is "neither before nor after" them. The mind was never essentially defiled: "what is defiled is, in its nature, ultimately pure." There are two liberations: from afflictions (the seeds ceasing) and from the things themselves (as the sūtra says: when craving for the eye is cut, the eye is cut). This is liberation with remainder; without remainder, it is "known by inner realisation", "simply the exhaustion of all suffering", "not mere non-existence", beyond every proliferation of same or different, existing or not after death.
**The last verse.** "In beings named as continua, and in the marks of dharmas, there is no transmigration in saṃsāra, and no one who enters nirvāṇa."

subs.head: A note on the last verse

blocks.text: The final verse is famous and easily misread. It does not deny saṃsāra and nirvāṇa as experiences. It denies that there is a *self* who wanders or a *self* who is liberated. What wanders is a continuum of conditioned dharmas; what is liberated is that continuum, released from affliction. This is the teaching of non-self carried to its conclusion, and it is why Venerable Miào Jìng insisted that liberation is not annihilation: the uncontaminated qualities remain; only the suffering, and the illusion of a sufferer, end.

quiz.q: The first verse's four lines answer which four objections?
options: no continuity of rebirth, simultaneous cause and effect, indiscriminate cause and effect, and retention without a cause
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The first is the objection that rebirth wouldn't continue; the second, that cause and effect would be simultaneous; the third, that any cause could yield any effect; the fourth, that retention has no cause."

quiz.q: "Shaped by what is taken up" — if there is no self, who takes it up? Which two readings does Master Cháng Bǎi list?
options: the Pixunji: self-view retains; Miào Jìng: the store-consciousness retains all karmic force — the English names no one
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Venerable Miào Jìng explains: since there is no self, who retains what is done? The store-consciousness retains all karmic force." The *Pixunji* says self-view does.

quiz.q: The English reads this verse as one causal chain. How do the lectures pair it?
options: two pairs: proliferation causes the ripened seed-body (projecting karma's result); pure and impure karma cause agreeable and disagreeable results (completing karma's: caste, looks, lifespan, wealth)
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Agreeable and disagreeable results are the differences gained from completing karma — caste, family, appearance, strength, lifespan, resources." The *Pixunji* separates the two causal pairs.

quiz.q: The English has ordinary beings "taking pleasant and unpleasant alike to be suffering." How does Venerable Miào Jìng punctuate the line?
options: "towards suffering one conceives self; experiencing pain and pleasure, one knows them as suffering" — a knowing to be cultivated
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Read this line as: towards suffering one reckons a self; feeling pain, feeling pleasure, one knows suffering." The knowing is bond-comprehension, a practice, not an ordinary error.

quiz.q: "When freed from afflictions, neither before nor after." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: manas isn't first and affliction later — they are simultaneous; the defiled mind arises and ceases with its four afflictions
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "It isn't that manas comes first and afflictions afterwards — they are simultaneous, hence 'not before.'" The English doesn't identify the defiled mind as manas.

quiz.q: "This freedom from defilement reveals two distinctions." The note says these are liberation with and without remainder. What do the treatise and lectures say?
options: liberation from affliction and liberation from the aggregates, both with remainder; the next verse turns to without remainder
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: no longer associated with affliction regarding the aggregates is liberation of the aggregates — faculties meet objects without affliction, and no future aggregate-result arises. The text then turns to the remainderless.
